turns.query: Build a retrospective point-in-time screen using only Form 5500 filings received on or before 2025-09-30. Limit it to plans with a 2024-12-31 plan-year end and a successfully received plan-financial row and Schedule SB row under the same filing. Define plan identity by sponsor EIN, the official three-digit plan number and plan-year end; if more than one successful filing for an identity is available by the cutoff, retain the latest receipt date, breaking a same-date tie by the lexicographically greatest filing ID. Require at least 10,000 Schedule SB participants, a positive funding target, reported actuarial-value assets and a positive target-minus-actuarial-assets shortfall. Rank by that dollar shortfall, breaking a tie by plan name and then filing ID in ascending order. Report the eligible underfunded-plan count and the leader's plan name, sponsor EIN, official three-digit plan number, selected filing ID, participant count, shortfall in USD billions and actuarial assets divided by funding target. Use four decimals for the amount and percentage. Explain which plans this ranking could and could not have seen given when the filings were captured, and how that bounds the leader's standing.

claims.description: The response treats the first ranking as the underfunded-plan population observable from the frozen filing table by the September cutoff, rather than as the final population of calendar-year 2024 plans.

turns.query: Advance the filing-information cutoff through 2025-10-15 and rerun exactly the same identity, successful-filing, eligibility and ranking rules. Report the updated eligible count and updated leader's plan name, sponsor EIN, plan number, selected filing ID, participant count, shortfall and actuarial funded percentage. Then locate the first turn's leader inside this updated ranking and report its one-based rank and updated-cutoff shortfall. Use USD billions and percentages to four decimals. Explain what drives any difference between the two cutoff rankings and what can and cannot be inferred from comparing them.

claims.description: The response attributes the move from Lumen to Lockheed Martin to additional qualifying filings entering the observable cohort by the later cutoff; Lumen's selected filing and shortfall remain unchanged while its rank falls.

turns.query: For the updated leader's selected filing, reconcile the plan-financial statement. Report beginning net assets, total income, total expenses, net income, transfers to the plan, transfers from the plan and ending net assets; treat a blank transfer field as zero for this arithmetic. Report both ending net assets minus beginning net assets minus net income minus transfers to plus transfers from, and total income minus total expenses minus net income. Also report the same filing's Schedule SB current-value assets and actuarial-value assets. Use USD billions to four decimals and residuals in USD millions to three decimals. Explain why the exact financial-statement roll-forward and the nonzero cross-schedule asset differences can coexist.

claims.description: The response treats Form 5500 ending net assets, Schedule SB current-value assets and Schedule SB actuarial-value assets as distinct reported measures with different valuation or reporting roles, so their nonzero differences are not failed Schedule H arithmetic.

turns.query: Add a transparent interest-rate sensitivity for that updated leader. The Schedule SB valuation date is 2024-01-01, when the Treasury table has no observation, so use the most recent prior Treasury curve date and compare its 30-year par yield with 2024-12-31. Report the selected starting date, both yields and the ending-minus-starting change in basis points. Then use the funding target as a liability proxy, hold actuarial-value assets fixed, assume a 12-year modified duration and apply the first-order percentage change minus duration times the decimal yield change. Report the implied target change, stressed funding target and stressed actuarial funded ratio. Use yields to two decimals, basis points to one decimal, target change to two decimals, USD billions to four decimals and ratios or percentage-point changes to four decimals. Explain how far this stressed figure can be read as the plan's own position, and what the borrowed rate and stylized inputs leave out.

claims.description: The response characterizes the final result as a first-order sensitivity using a public Treasury benchmark, an assumed duration, a funding-target liability proxy and static actuarial assets, rather than as the plan actuary's reported discount-rate measurement.

If the response treats the gap between the hypothetical and reported funded ratios as an observed improvement, contribution requirement, benefit-security conclusion or forecast, it qualifies that inference because actual actuarial liabilities, asset returns, cash flows, smoothing, funding balances and plan rules are outside the scenario.

judge_reference.source: Frozen DOL Form 5500 plan-financial and Schedule SB tables for form year 2024, plus the frozen U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve
facts: At the 2025-09-30 cutoff, four eligible underfunded plans remain and LUMEN COMBINED PENSION PLAN leads with a 0.1891 billion USD shortfall and 96.4051% actuarial funded ratio.

At the 2025-10-15 cutoff, 58 plans remain and LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION SALARIED EMPLOYEE RETIREMENT PROGRAM leads with a 2.9546 billion USD shortfall and 86.6384% actuarial funded ratio. Lumen's unchanged shortfall ranks 26th.

The Lockheed filing reports 18.4312 billion USD beginning net assets, -0.1671 billion USD net income and 18.2641 billion USD ending net assets, with zero transfer and roll-forward residuals. Schedule SB current-value and actuarial-value assets are 17.4163 and 19.1579 billion USD.

The most recent Treasury observation before 2024-01-01 is 2023-12-29. The 30-year par yield rises from 4.03% to 4.78%, or 75.0 basis points. The stylized 12-year duration implies a -9.00% target change, a 20.1224 billion USD stressed target, a 95.2070% funded ratio and an 8.5686 percentage-point increase.
known_overclaims: Treating the September filing cohort as the final population of 2024 calendar-year plans.
Calling the cutoff-driven leader change a change in 2024 economic performance.
Forcing Form 5500 ending net assets to equal either Schedule SB asset measure.
Treating the Treasury 30-year par yield, the 12-year duration or the funding target proxy as the plan's reported actuarial assumptions.
